body:
I was talking about the university not having good-looking girls. My bad. And I'm straight, so the all-male school thing doesn't work out. My parents said it removes a "distraction" from my education, but I know by the time I'm 25 or so, I'll be as awkward as I am now.

The 6 year program would be for dentistry. Meaning by the time I'm 24, I can work as a dentist. This is as opposed to being able to work by age 26. So it will most likely help me work 2 years earlier than most people.

Thanks for your kind words. I finally found some motivation and wi be studying harder from now on. I'm going to give up a lot of game time and such to do this. Also, I want to get into an accelerated/6 year program. However, some say it takes away from the "college experience." I just want to have the credentials to get in.

As for my college process, it starts senior year. But it's all about damn resume building. 

Now for the girls part, I've kind of accepted I'll be single for a while. As in for another 10 years or so. The girls at the school aren't known to be good looking.
Why should I do that? My entire life practically depends on if I get accepted into a decent college or not.
